properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 26 at 11:55PM MDT until October 27 at 11:45AM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northeastern Conejos County in south central Colorado...
West Central Costilla County in south central Colorado...
Southeastern Rio Grande County in south central Colorado...
Southwestern Alamosa County in southeastern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 1145 AM MDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Widespread
inundation of agriculture fields, wetlands, and other low-lying
areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1155 PM MDT, Gauge reports continue to indicate high stream
flows. Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly in the
warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Alamosa, San Luis Valley Airport, Sanford, La Jara and Alamosa
East.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.areaDesc: Alamosa, CO; Conejos, CO; Costilla, CO; Rio Grande, CO

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 26 at 9:42PM MDT until October 27 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Colorado...

Rio Grande At Alamosa affecting Alamosa County.

For the Upper Rio Grande...including Alamosa...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Grande at Alamosa.

* WHEN...Until Tuesday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 9.0 feet, Minor flooding. Minor agricultural flooding
in low lying areas along the river

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:30 PM MDT Monday the stage was 9.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 7.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:30 PM MDT Monday was 9.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall to 4 feet by 1 pm Monday
afternoon.
- Flood stage is 9.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 9.3
feet on 05/18/1944.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 26 at 7:03PM MDT until October 29 at 4:00AM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Pueblo has issued a Flood Warning
for the following rivers in Colorado...

Purgatoire River Near Las Animas affecting Bent County.

For the Purgatoire River...including Las Animas...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...High flow is traveling down the Upper Purgatoire from recent
rains, and may lead to flooding near Las Animas.

* WHERE...Purgatoire River near Las Animas.

* WHEN...From late tonight to late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...At 9.0 feet, Minor Flood. Minor agricultural flooding
occurs into low lying areas along the river.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 6:15 PM MDT Monday the stage was 6.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 7.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage just
after midnight tonight to a crest of 10.5 feet tomorrow evening.
It will then fall below flood stage Wednesday afternoon.
- Flood stage is 9.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 10.5
feet on 08/19/2004.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 25 at 9:00AM MDT until October 27 at 9:00AM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall which occurred over
the last couple of days is expected or ongoing.

* WHERE...Northeastern Conejos County in south central Colorado...
Southwestern Alamosa County in southeastern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 900 AM MDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding will occur in low-lying and flood-prone
locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 852 AM MDT, flooding was occurring along the Rio Grande River
in low lying and agricultural areas. This high water is due to
all of the heavy rain which occurred over the last couple of
days.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include low lying
areas in parts of Alamosa and parts of Conejos counties.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
